rationale: This is a pure 2x2 recombination of two archive signals (HardBookDislocationCleanCheap and OwnHistoryCheapWithQuality) differing by a single operator swap (MIN→SUMRANK), which is exactly the cosmetic-variant consolidation the objective warns against and adds no new economic claim.

The stated mechanism — strip leverage amplification to price the *business* — is not what the expression computes, since it puts book *equity* over *enterprise* value, a numerator/denominator mismatch that mechanically penalizes levered firms rather than neutralizing leverage (the coherent version would use invested capital or total assets in the numerator).

A legitimately motivated coverage repair that re-derives the highest-alpha quality channel from densely reported balance-sheet items, though the two legs (count of WC decreases and the WC/sales trend) are built from the same underlying series and are likely substantially redundant, which caps the expected information gain.

Testing the second moment of the accrual process alongside its trend is an economically distinct dimension (Dechow-Dichev-style accrual quality) that has only been tested under a contaminated amplifier, so the retest is defensible — but both legs derive from the same non-cash-WC/sales series, so the added dimension may be largely mechanical rather than informational.

Equal-weighting the externally verified tax leg is a substantively different quality channel with independent prior Fama-MacBeth support and an untested weighting, though the txp/at level is a stale, industry- and size-confounded proxy for tax verification and this remains one of three near-identical hard-book/SUMRANK cells proposed in the same batch.

MA(COALESCE(dvc,0)/at,3) is dominated by the payer/non-payer split, making the quality leg effectively a dividend-payer dummy and the signal a rediscovery of the well-documented payout/dividend-premium-in-value effect; moreover dividends can be debt-financed, so they are weak evidence that *earnings* are cash-backed.
